title: Path of Exile 2 0.3.1 Endgame Tablet Rework: Map Device Use, Three-Slot Limit & Tower's New Role
summary: 0.3.1 reworked the Endgame Tablet system: Tablets no longer go in Towers, are used directly in the Map Device with a fixed use count, and a single Map can take up to three Tablets based on its Mod count. This page explains the old vs new flow and which Atlas guides are outdated.
description: A high-intent history of the 0.3.1 Endgame Tablet rework: why Tablets left the Tower, how they are now used in the Map Device, the fixed-use and three-slot rules, what Towers still do, and an audit of outdated Atlas farming guides.
author: StratLore Editorial
imageAlt: The Master's Reach, an Endgame-influenced unique item

sections.title: Quick summary
paragraphs: 0.3.1 delivered a high-impact rework of the Endgame Tablet system. Before 0.3.1, Tablets were placed into Towers; after 0.3.1, they are used directly in the Map Device, have a fixed number of uses, and a single Map can carry up to three Tablets with the slot count tied to the Map's Mod count.
Towers did not disappear: they still provide Atlas vision and reward duties, but the 'put the Tablet in the Tower' workflow that old guides describe is gone.
bullets: Tablets no longer placed in Towers.
Used directly in the Map Device.
Fixed number of uses per Tablet.
One Map up to three Tablets; slots scale with Map Mod count.
Towers keep Atlas vision and rewards.
0.3.1 also shipped boss, performance, item UI and bug fixes.

sections.title: Old flow (pre-0.3.1)
sections.oldText: Acquire a Tablet, place it into a Tower, and the Tower's radius applied the Tablet's effect to maps in range.
sections.newText: Use the Tablet directly in the Map Device on a specific Map; it has a fixed use count and the Map can hold up to three Tablets based on its Mod count.

changes.title: Tablet in Map Device
changes.detail: Tablets are now applied to a chosen Map via the Map Device rather than a Tower.

changes.title: Fixed use count
changes.detail: Each Tablet has a fixed number of uses instead of an infinite Tower radius.

changes.title: Up to three Tablets per Map
changes.detail: A single Map can use up to three Tablets; the available slot count depends on the Map's Mod count.

changes.title: Tower role retained
changes.detail: Towers continue to provide Atlas vision and reward duties; they are no longer the Tablet container.

cards.detail: A Map's Tablet slot count is determined by its number of Mods; more Mods can mean more slots, up to three.
Each Tablet is consumed over a fixed number of map uses; plan batches accordingly.
Towers still grant Atlas vision and reward coverage; pair them with Map-Device Tablets.

items.question: Do I still put Tablets in Towers?
answer: No. Since 0.3.1, Tablets are used directly in the Map Device, not placed in Towers. Towers now only provide Atlas vision and rewards.

items.question: How many Tablets can one Map take?
answer: Up to three, and the number of available slots depends on the Map's Mod count.

items.question: Do Tablets last forever now?
answer: No. Each Tablet has a fixed number of uses; it is consumed over those uses rather than applying infinitely via a Tower radius.
